interfaces.name: Stone-crush roots
interfaces.function: Use actual reusable stone and bark to crush roots for later eating, conserving nutrients and age.
interfaces.costs: One actual stone and bark are reserved reusable implements; prepare 1–4 owned roots with two rounds per raw root, one energy per round. Defaults to a nearby eastward worksite; explicit x/y select another actual site. No silent relocation if blocked. New assess-surface/prepare-small operations require separate root-preparation-surface mastery; legacy prepare retains its whole-unit inputs and existing costs.
interfaces.effects: Preserve mass, nutrients, toxicity and accumulated spoilage. Crushed food ages at 1.25 baseline. Partial cancellation retains its actual processing fraction and age. No cooking or preservation benefit is implied.

execution.progress: Exact processId, actual site, escrow, reusable tools, paid energy and remaining work. Continue resumes; changing actions or lost reach pauses. Cancel/death releases actual material once without effort refunds.

interfaces.name: Assess and peel actual branch bark
interfaces.function: Assess actual materials and separate a finite branch outer layer using a personally inspected reusable stone or flint contact.
interfaces.costs: Assess: one round and 0.2 energy. Peel: two active work-round equivalents and two energy per original branch unit, proportionally less for fractional or partly peeled inputs; one final partial simulation round pays only remaining effort. Reserve actual source and one reusable inspected hard stone/flint. No hard inventory capacity exists; actual load costs continue.
interfaces.effects: Standing trunks without represented tissue remain ineligible. Unspecified intact branch partitions at most 10% of existing mass into outer bark. Exact-tenth bark units round down; sub-unit mass stays bark-fines. Peeled core cannot satisfy intact-branch recipes. Existing composition, nutrients, toxins, fuel and age persist. Cancellation/death releases actual partial materials once. Assessment alone has no reward; a new verified paid separation can use existing grounded understanding.

execution.progress: Exact personal processId, paid and remaining effort, reserved tool, actual separated mass and residual layer. Reissue peel with processId to resume. Other actions pause; cancel/death terminates without refund.

interfaces.name: Assess and use a fractional root-preparation surface
interfaces.function: Assess the actual connected bark rectangle and hard tool on firm support, then prepare at most one root using that physically sufficient sheet.
interfaces.costs: Separately learn this extension after root-preparation. assess-surface: barkId, toolId and optional site{x,y}, one round and 0.2 energy. prepare-small: assessed barkId, toolId, rootId, quantity in exact tenths from 0.1 to 1, and optional site. Reserve only that root portion, the whole selected sheet and one reusable stone. Two work equivalents and two energy per original root; a fractional final increment costs only remaining work. Continue/status/cancel name processId.
interfaces.effects: One connected rectangle at least 0.16 by 0.16 m contains food on firm support; a single unfragmented extracted bark lot may use explicitly uncertain mass-conserving model geometry at density 500 and thickness 0.003, unless represented geometry exists. Separate combined lots and fines are not joined sheets. Actual stone hardness >=3, flexible intact sheet, clear reachable site and energy are required. Processing conserves nutrition, toxins, mass and age; crushed food ages at 1.25 baseline. Lost access pauses without work while food ages. Cancel/death releases actual partial food and implements once. No nutrition, preservation or safety benefit is inferred.

execution.progress: Actual processId, selected root quantity, sheet geometry basis, paid fractional work/energy, remaining work and pause reason. No second reservation while continuing.

personalIntent.reason: The tick-102 assessment recorded unsuitable equipment despite modelled sheet dimensions exceeding the required footprint. The limiting condition is not yet known.
personalIntent.progress: Health is 100 and satiety 65.5. I own the bark sheet and stone, but have no root and no successful surface assessment.
personalIntent.next: Recover energy, inspect the actual stone, then reassess the implements at my current site.
personalIntent.pause: Do not attempt food preparation until the actual setup passes assessment.

shown.question: Which actual condition prevents my bark-and-stone setup from supporting small-batch root preparation?
evidence: The assessment model gives one connected 0.3 by 0.2 m bark sheet; dimensions are explicitly model-derived, not measured.
The required food footprint is 0.16 by 0.16 m.
shown.uncertainty: The limiting tool, sheet or support condition is unresolved.
shown.goal: Identify the failed physical requirement before obtaining a root for a preparation trial.
completedSteps: Performed a surface assessment; the setup was unsuitable.
outputs: Retained separated bark sheet, stone, peeled core and bark fines.
Recorded an unsuccessful physical suitability assessment.
shown.missing: An identified limiting condition and a successful setup assessment.
shown.next: Inspect the stone and reassess the actual setup.
shown.benefit: The failed assessment establishes that preparation should not yet proceed.

shown.method: Paid assessment of actual material using retained or explicitly modelled geometry
shown.condition: A containing sheet on firm support, not freestanding impact support. Dimensions retain their stated uncertainty.

shown.subject: Tested branch bark separation
shown.text: I have physically peeled gathered branches using an inspected stone. Paid trials confirmed a separable outer layer, at most 10% of original mass; this yields small bark quantities plus fines. I have not yet built or tested a drying tray, and cannot claim preservation benefits.

shown.subject: Verified branch peeling result
shown.text: I completed paid branch peeling with my inspected stone. One branch yielded 0.3 bark units, bark fines and a peeled core; personal trial confirmed separation. I have not yet verified whether that fractional bark stack suffices for root preparation.

shown.subject: Preservation materials
shown.text: I have not located stone or bark. I learned root air drying: its tray needs two stone and one bark, and drying is slow and weather-dependent. I will inspect a nearby tree and explore a short distance east for materials; no preservation result yet.

shown: Tick 102 assessed this setup as unsuitable; adequate modelled sheet dimensions alone do not establish suitability.
Berries and roots have personally observed zero toxicity and nutrition of 8 and 14 respectively.
Crushing is not preservation and does not remove toxins.
